title: Session affinity fallback and observability adapter integration
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
This guide describes the integration pattern and operational playbook for Session Affinity Fallback paired with the Observability Adapter. The goal is to maintain per-tenant session continuity (sticky routing + KV cache coherence) during model rollouts, capacity surges, and cross-environment (hosted -> dedicated -> private) handoffs while preserving telemetry fidelity for QBRs and incident investigations.

Context and problem statement
- Customers expect conversational continuity: the same persona, context, and KV cache should follow a tenant’s session even if the request is routed to a fallback or alternate deployment.
- During capacity pressure, routing changes, or version rollouts, naive failover breaks KV caches and makes tracing and quality regression analysis difficult.
- We provide an Observability Adapter that adds tenant-level metadata and reconciles distributed KV cache ownership during handoffs. This document explains the integration steps, config, and runbook for failure modes.

When to use
1) Enterprise tenants with strong SLAs for session continuity and traceable outputs.
2) Migration windows between hosted and dedicated/private deployments.
3) Canary or canary-surge auto-failovers where preserving context reduces user-facing quality regressions.

Architecture overview (text diagram)
- Client -> Ingress-proxy (sticky cookie / token) -> Routing-orchestrator -> [Primary pool: tenant-gateway -> model-pool, KV-store primary]
                                                                                                                        -> [Fallback pool: tenant-proxy -> model-pool, KV-sync sidecar]
- Observability Adapter (obs-adapter) is a sidecar in front of forwarders and emits tenant-scoped traces/metrics to the telemetry pipeline.
- KV-sync replicates prefix caches (KV cache) with configurable staleness windows.

Key components and responsibilities
- ingress-proxy: issues session tokens, enforces affinity hints (cookie, JWT claim), and marks requests with affinity headers. Owner: ingress team.
- routing-orchestrator: evaluates routing policy (latency vs cost vs tier) and decides fallback targets. Owner: routing team.
- tenant-gateway: primary request path for tenant; keeps authoritative KV ownership. Owner: tenant-platform.
- tenant-proxy + kv-sync sidecar: receives handoff requests; kv-sync attempts prefix/KV reconciliation with primary. Owner: private-deployments / dedicated ops.
- obs-adapter: injects tenant_id, session_id, model_version, fallback_reason into spans/metrics and emits structured logs for the QBR pipeline. Owner: telemetry team.

Prerequisites
- Tenant has a session token flow (cookie or bearer token) and tenant_id is present in request.
- KV sync endpoints enabled with TLS between primary and fallback pools.
- Observability Adapter image version >= 2.3.0 deployed alongside ingress-proxy and tenant-proxy.
- Routing-orchestrator supports fallback_reason codes and an affinity header (X-Redwood-Affinity).

Configuration examples
1) ingress-proxy affinity cookie (snippet):
- cookie_name: rw_session
- ttl: 3600 # seconds
- secure: true
- same_site: Lax

2) routing-orchestrator policy (YAML):
policy:
  - name: preserve-affinity-on-surge
    priority: 10
    conditions:
      - type: capacity-pressure
        threshold: 0.85
    actions:
      - type: fallback
        target_pool: fallback-pool-us-west
        preserve_affinity: true
        kv_reconciliation_window_sec: 30

3) kv-sync sidecar config (JSON example):
{
  "mode": "incremental",
  "max_prefix_bytes": 524288,
  "staleness_ttl_sec": 60,
  "consistency": "eventual",
  "reconciliation_interval_sec": 15
}

4) obs-adapter injection config (snippet):
- obs_adapter:
    emit_span_tags: ["tenant_id","session_id","model_variant","fallback_reason"]
    redact_fields: ["user_message.pii"]
    sample_rate: 1.0

Integration steps (high level)
1) Deploy obs-adapter v2.3.0 to ingress-proxy and tenant-proxy pods. Verify sidecar readiness.
2) Enable X-Redwood-Affinity header in ingress-proxy and set preserve_affinity: true in the routing-orchestrator policy used for the tenant.
3) Configure kv-sync TLS trust between primary and fallback clusters. Exchange certs using the private-deployments onboarding script.
4) Start a staged rollout: 10% traffic to fallback-pool with preserve_affinity and kv_reconciliation_window_sec=60.
5) Validate session continuity using the QA checklist below and observe traces in the telemetry dashboard.

QA and verification checklist
- Create a multi-turn session (10 turns) and note session_id.
- Force a controlled failover via routing-orchestrator API:
  curl -X POST "https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/fallback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"tenant_id":"acme-corp","target":"fallback-pool-us-west","force":true}'
- Confirm the session_id is preserved in returned response headers (X-Session-Id).
- Inspect obs-adapter spans in Grafana/Tempo: ensure span tags contain tenant_id/model_variant/fallback_reason.
- Compare the produced response tokenization metadata for parity between primary and fallback (embedding dimensions, top-p, temperature).

Monitoring, alerts, and SLOs
- Telemetry emitted by obs-adapter: metric rw.session.handoff.count, rw.kv.reconciliation.success_rate, rw.handoff.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99).
- Recommended alert thresholds (pager):
  - rw.kv.reconciliation.success_rate < 95% for 5m -> page oncall (severity P1).
  - rw.handoff.latency_ms.p95 > 400ms for 10m -> notify routing and tenant-platform (P2).
  - rw.session.handoff.count spikes > 3x baseline per 5m -> alert capacity ops (P2).
- SLO targets for enterprise tenants using affinity:
  - Session continuity (session-id preserved across handoff): 99.9% monthly.
  - KV reconciliation success rate: 99% monthly.
  - Handoff latency p95: < 350ms.

Failure modes and runbook (step-by-step)
1) Symptom: KV_sync failing (error logs show TLS handshake failures) Runbook:
  a) Check kv-sync sidecar logs on fallback node: kubectl -n tenant-proxy logs -l app=kv-sync
  b) Validate TLS cert expiry: kubectl -n certs get secret tenant-kv-tls -o yaml | grep expiration
  c) If cert expired, follow cert-rotation playbook: update secret with new cert and restart pods.
  d) If network policy blocking, verify CNI rules and peering: run traceroute from fallback to primary on port 9200.

2) Symptom: Session ID not preserved after failover Runbook:
  a) Verify ingress-proxy is propagating X-Session-Id header.
  b) Inspect routing-orchestrator logs for preserve_affinity evaluation.
  c) If preserve_affinity=false, verify policy matches tenant label (policy may be scoped to enterprise-tier).
  d) If header present but lost downstream, check tenant-proxy header whitelist. Add X-Session-Id to allowed list.

3) Symptom: Observability spans missing tenant tags Runbook:
  a) Confirm obs-adapter sidecar is running and healthy. kubectl -n ingress get pods -l app=obs-adapter
  b) Check obs-adapter config: emit_span_tags includes tenant_id and session_id.
  c) If sample_rate < 1.0, temporarily set to 1.0 for a diagnostics window.

Rollout checklist and rollback plan
- Rollout (canary):
  1) Deploy obs-adapter to staging and run synthetic multi-turn sessions.
  2) Enable preserve_affinity for 5% of traffic to fallback. Monitor kv_reconciliation.success_rate and rw.session.handoff.count for 30 minutes.
  3) Increase to 25% if metrics stable.
  4) After 2 hours at 25% and no P1s, expand to 100% for tenant.
- Rollback:
  - Immediate rollback: set routing-orchestrator policy to disable fallback (preserve_affinity=false) and redirect traffic to primary only.
  - If KV divergence occurred, run kv-sync reconciliation job with mode=full-sync (may incur cost/time). Track reconciliation job via job id returned by API.

Ownership and contacts
- Oncall (first-line): Customer Success Oncall (cs-oncall@redwood.ai)
- Escalation (P2+): Routing team (routing-eng@redwood.ai), Tenant Platform (tenant-platform@redwood.ai)
- Telemetry debugging: telemetry-observability@redwood.ai

Testing matrix for enterprise scenarios
- Scenario A: small multi-turn chat with immediate failover -> expected: session preserved, p95 latency increase < 150ms
- Scenario B: long context completion (2k tokens) with fallback -> expected: responses aligned but may have reduced caching efficiency; run embedding parity check post-handoff
- Scenario C: cross-region handoff (us-east -> eu-west) -> expected: increased latency but KV-sync allowed with staleness_ttl_sec >= 120

Operational notes and tips
- Prefer incremental kv-sync for low-latency workloads; schedule full-sync during maintenance windows.
- Use the obs-adapter structured logs to drive automated QBR sampling: tag sessions with product_feature and sample by tenant_impact_score.
- For private deployments behind air-gapped networks, provide a signed cert bundle using the private-deployments onboarding tool: scripts/certs/generate-bundle.sh

References and related pages
- routing policy reference: /confluence/eng-platform/routing-policy-reference
- kv-sync architecture: /confluence/eng-infra/gpu-fleet-and-capacity/kv-sync-architecture
- obs-adapter telemetry schema: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/obs-adapter-schema

Appendix: useful CLI snippets
- Force canary fallback via orchestrator:
  curl -X POST "https://orchestrator.internal/api/v1/fallback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"tenant_id":"acme-corp","target":"fallback-pool-us-west","preserve_affinity":true}'

- Inspect reconciliation job status:
  curl -s "https://kv-sync.internal/api/v1/reconcile?job_id=JOB12345" -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_ADMIN_TOKEN" | jq

- Quick validation script (python):
  python - <<'PY'
  import requests
  headers = {"Authorization":"Bearer $RW_ADMIN_TOKEN","Content-Type":"application/json"}
  r = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat", headers=headers, json={"tenant_id":"acme-corp","session_id":"test-123","input":"hello"})
  print(r.headers.get('X-Session-Id'), r.json().get('response'))
  PY

Document lifecycle and maintenance
- Owners must review this guide quarterly or after any obs-adapter, routing-orchestrator, or kv-sync release.
- Major changes to preserve_affinity semantics require an update to enterprise SLOs and customer-facing documentation.

Feedback and improvements
- For integration gaps or missing telemetry fields, open an internal ticket in the #obs-adapter Slack channel and link the ticket to this page.
- Suggested improvements: automatic prefix reconciliation metrics per-session, stronger guarantees for bounded staleness in dedicated-private handoffs.
